hypnosis_quote: The longer version of this exercise can be found in my Inner Child Self-Love Reparenting Guide .
source_quote: Maybe you copy one small thing you’ve seen them do, or imagine them there when they’re not, and try one piece yourself while they’re still helping with the rest. That’s what I mean by borrowed adulthood.
why: The reader is sent to the Inner Child guide for a longer version of the hat exercise, but that guide no longer has the adult hat, the apprentice adult or the step of returning the hat; it now describes borrowing as someone doing part of the adult role with you first while you copy one piece, and as five stages (S004).
what: The pointer sentence in S019, and whether the hat steps stay as the hypnosis guide's own.

hypnosis_quote: I’m not saying you should use substances, but many people have used them when they first did self-hypnosis, contacted their inner child, or talked to their Higher Self.
source_heading: If a past trip went badly
source_quote: If you go manic, psychotic (by which I mean losing your sense of reality to the point of posing a risk to yourself or others), get super paranoid, or end up worse afterward than before, those are signs to reconsider trying the same thing again, and try to figure out why that happened. Don’t try again until you understand what would make it safe.
why: A reader who mixes substances with this work is told to start sober and what not to use self-hypnosis for, but not the signs that mean stop and don't repeat it (mania, psychosis, strong paranoia, ending up worse), nor when to see a professional, all of which the source now spells out.
what: After the first paragraph of S136; point to source S101 to S108 (Losing Touch With Reality). Check the hypnosis guide's own safety sections first; they weren't in the file I was given.

hypnosis_quote: Just not hitting back is enough to start being the adult, even if it isn't enough yet for them to trust you. Even that takes some warmth, and if you don't have any yet, borrow some from someone who's been good to you, or from an adult you imagine.
source_quote: That’s enough to start being the adult, even if it isn’t enough yet for them to trust you. That takes warmth, and if there isn’t any yet, borrow some.
why: The hypnosis guide says even not hitting back takes warmth, while the source says you can stop judging with no love coming yet and that it is trust that takes warmth, so a reader with no warmth yet is given a higher bar for the first step than the source sets.
what: The sentence starting 'Even that takes some warmth' in S021: what 'that' points to.

hypnosis_quote: If you feel resistance, just meet it with love. If you feel or see something, just meet that with love as well.
source_quote: They might go numb, or call BS on that. If so, they might just need to see if you’re actually humble enough, and grateful enough for them, to listen to their rejection, be patient, and be open to the possibility that your Higher View is missing the trees for the forest.
why: Told to meet resistance with love, a reader can keep sending love at a part that is refusing it, where the source no longer says that and instead says to listen to the refusal, be patient and allow that the higher view is missing something.
what: The two 'meet it with love' sentences in the third paragraph of S024.

hypnosis_quote: And I don’t think the Higher Self has any specific wisdom.
source_quote: But where I part ways with IFS is I don’t think the Higher Self has any specific wisdom that can be followed mechanically.
why: Read flat, the sentence says the Higher Self has no wisdom, two paragraphs after a script that asks it for help; the source limits the claim to wisdom that can be followed mechanically and, two sentences on, names leaving all decisions to the Higher Self as spiritual bypassing.
what: The 'any specific wisdom' sentence in S017.

hypnosis_quote: When something specific comes up, that’s the time to sort out what it is.
source_quote: I wouldn’t spend long deciding what to call each part you meet.
why: The hypnosis guide gives a reader who already splits into too many parts seven sorting questions, while the source now says not to spend long naming a part and to ask what it wants before deciding where it comes from.
what: The last paragraph of S017 (the 'sort out what it is' sentence and its questions); source S064 and S074 say the same as S070.

hypnosis_quote: Start with whatever adult function you can connect to, but most of us need enough Nurturer and Protector first, before the Guide.
source_quote: While all of these super powers should be developed alongside each other, the inner child’s receptivity will naturally follow this order: first he/she wants to feel safe (Protector), then, building on that safety, feel loved (Nurturer), and then building on the safety & love, trust allows the little one to be eager to take guidance, and that’s where Guide-building comes in.
why: The hypnosis guide puts the Nurturer section before the Protector and treats the two as one step before the Guide, while the source now gives an order (safety first, then love, then guidance) and lays its sections out that way, so a reader may start with warmth the inner child can't take in yet.
what: The order sentence in the last paragraph of S027, and whether S025 and S026 swap places.

hypnosis_quote: Ask them for help with directing your life.
source_quote: As the Guide, you choose what your little one learns and what it gets to experience, and you hold standards, the way a good parent would.
why: The hypnosis guide has the reader ask the Guide for direction as if it were someone else, while the source makes the Guide a job the reader does (as the hypnosis guide itself does for the Nurturer and Protector), and in trance an inner figure's answers are easier to take as orders.
what: The first two paragraphs of S027 ('work with your Guide', 'Ask them for help'); this may be meant for hypnosis.

hypnosis_quote: Often this script acts as a critic or warden, telling your inner child not to cry or complain.
source_quote: Keep in mind that while a critical voice might be that inherited parent script, or any outside influence with no concern for your welfare, it could also be trying to protect you from rejection or failure. It may be pointing to a real problem, but in a cruel way.
why: The reader learns to see the inherited script only as a critic to answer back, and misses the source's point that a critical voice may be trying to protect them or pointing at a real problem, to be heard for what is true in it without taking the cruelty.
what: After the 'critic or warden' sentence in S029, and in the parent-script paragraph of S070; source S028 (Reframe the Critic) has the how.

hypnosis_quote: Still, notice it, and then look at what might be going on.
source_quote: Let a stray thought go as just thinking, and come back to the room you’re in. A worry that just keeps asking to be reassured can go the same way, unless it’s your little one asking.
why: The hypnosis guide says to look into each distraction or objection, while the source now says to let a stray thought go, and a worry that only wants reassurance too, which keeps a reader from feeding a reassurance loop.
what: The last sentence of the first paragraph of S028.

hypnosis_quote: G. Stop and rest before the caring turns into another performance, and reconnect with them later to see what was helpful.
source_quote: Going back to reconnect with your little one is normal parenting/reparenting, but returning to lick the same wound over and over can become a search for certainty in an inherently uncertain existence.
why: The steps tell the reader to come back and see what helped, with no warning that going back to the same wound again and again can turn into checking for certainty, or that a practice which feels like a ritual to finish before living should stop.
what: Step G of S032; source S089 ends on the stop rule.

hypnosis_quote: A. Prepare yourself to tend to them with some privacy, but still able to access support if needed.
source_quote: If being alone was a big part of what hurt during your childhood, I’d call somebody now, mess and all, since reaching toward people is part of taking care of your little one too. Even if you don’t have someone you know who wants to listen, there are warmlines for this (not hotlines unless it’s an emergency).
why: A reader whose childhood hurt was being left alone is told to prepare some privacy with support in reach, where the source now says to call somebody first, a warmline if there is no one.
what: Step A of S032, after the privacy and support sentence.

hypnosis_quote: Even if there isn’t a child part that you can talk to, you can work with whatever you are aware of.
source_quote: If you don’t hear a little kid talking in your head, don’t invent one. Actually, this is one place where the usual inner-child prompt to “ask your little one what they need” can get confusing, because “ask” sounds like you’re supposed to ask a question and then wait for a second voice to answer.
why: A reader who hears no inner voice is told to work with what they're aware of but not warned against making up a child's voice, and the guide's many 'ask them' steps can read as waiting for a second voice to reply.
what: S072, and the 'ask' wording in step C of S032; source S067 also allows just knowing, or guessing, without an answer.

hypnosis_quote: There may not be an answer that will help you.
source_heading: If it tells you to act
source_quote: I’d only do it if it’s loving and leaves you free. It should make sense, too. Even then, anything big or hard to undo can wait until you’re calm and you’ve checked it against what you actually know.
why: The section covers getting no answer but not what to do when an answer tells the reader to act, where the source now gives a test (loving, leaves you free, makes sense) and says anything big or hard to undo waits.
what: End of S071, unless Appendix F's other sections (not in the file I was given) already say it; source S098 adds what to do when a voice or urge points toward harm.

hypnosis_quote: It can be an image, a posture, a voice, a memory, an emotion, etc.
source_quote: Old memories might come up too. They can feel totally real, but that alone doesn’t prove they happened.
why: The section says the inner child may show up as a memory, and nothing in the sections I was given tells the reader that a memory which feels real in an altered state isn't proof that it happened.
what: After the 'any form' sentences in S031, unless the guide's own section on memory (not in the file I was given) already says it; source S068 adds not to accuse anyone on that basis.

hypnosis_quote: Seeking counsel can slide into abdicating to an authority figure without you noticing.
source_quote: But they can know things you don’t and still be wrong for you to follow too much. The test is whether the relationship makes you more grounded, truthful, and free.
why: The reader is warned that taking counsel can slide into handing power to an authority 'without you noticing' and is given no way to notice, where the source now has a test for the person you lean on (and whether they respect a no) and a list of manipulation signs.
what: After the 'abdicating' sentence in S133, and the 'safe adult' sentence in S019; the signs list (source S020) by link.

hypnosis_quote: It has to come from a place of understanding, otherwise it can be bypassing.
source_quote: And you don’t have to forgive first to get safe, set boundaries, hold someone accountable, get justice or get better.
why: A reader can take the passage to mean that getting safe or getting better waits on forgiving, which the source now rules out in so many words.
what: After the second sentence of S134.

hypnosis_quote: The sequence for doing this with borrowed adulthood and the arrangement of 3 functions of adulthood , etc, is not from these authors, however.
source_quote: My inner child reparenting framework developed through the teachers and collaborators credited below and my own practice.
why: The sources note says who the three adult functions are not from and stops there, while the source now credits them: Daja's work for the Nurturer and Protector, Key for adding the Guide (S153, S003).
what: The last sentence of S162.

hypnosis_quote: Tell me what feels unsafe.
source_quote: Tell me what makes the love feel unreal to you.
why: The same script ends on a different question in each guide: the hypnosis guide asks what feels unsafe, the source asks what makes the love feel unreal, which answers the child's 'I don't believe you' more directly.
what: The last sentence of the script in S021.

hypnosis_quote: What's going on?
source_quote: What can we work on together?
why: The same script ends on a different question in each guide; the source's invites the part to work with the reader, where the hypnosis guide's asks it to explain itself.
what: The question that ends the script in the fourth paragraph of S028.

hypnosis_quote: The two-hand practice
source_quote: A Heart to Child Loop
why: A reader who goes from one guide to the other looking for the same practice finds it under another name.
what: The name in the heading of S024 and in S127.

hypnosis_quote: They may be younger than you are now. Both talk in your grown-up voice, so to your little one they're the same.
source_quote: The resentment can be purely visceral: being doubted after you’ve tried feels unfair, but there’s nothing unfair in them checking if you’re really gonna be the rock they need.
why: The two sentences are hard to follow (who 'they' are, and why their age matters), where the source now says what the second voice is, resentment at being doubted, and that the child's checking is fair.
what: The 'They may be younger' and 'Both talk' sentences in S022.

hypnosis_quote: Even if you feel like you already know what they need, ask if they'd prefer warmth, space, verbal reassurance, silence, distance, whatever.
source_quote: Not that you have to make a ritual of asking every time, if it’s obvious what they want.
why: The hypnosis guide says to ask even when you think you know what they need, and the source now says asking needn't become a ritual when it's obvious.
what: The second sentence of step C in S032.

hypnosis_quote: Every so often, come back to how you got to be someone who could do that, until you understand the pattern well enough that it can't drive you anymore.
source_quote: Then you’re allowed to stop holding yourself hostage, and the responsibility stays.
why: The hypnosis guide ends self-forgiveness on coming back to the fault every so often, which the source doesn't say: it ends on being allowed to stop, and elsewhere (S088) warns against returning to the same wound to check it.
what: The last sentence of S135.

hypnosis_quote: Even that takes some warmth, and if you don't have any yet, borrow some from someone who's been good to you, or from an adult you imagine.
source_quote: Just feel that love you can feel for others for a minute, in your body, before you try to redirect anything.
why: The reader with nobody who has been good to them is offered only an imagined adult, and misses the source's third lender: the love they already give someone else, felt first and then turned toward the child.
what: After the 'borrow some' sentence in S021.

hypnosis_quote: Only say the "I love you" part if you can feel it. If you don't feel the love yet, say you care.
source_quote: And if “I love you” goes flat when said to yourself or your little one, the same goodwill wish can be a stabler place to start.
why: When 'I love you' isn't true yet the hypnosis guide says to say you care, and the source now offers a goodwill wish ('May you be loving, peaceful, and free') as the steadier thing to say.
what: The last two sentences of S034.

hypnosis_quote: Without the Guide, you can also slide from looking after your inner child into spoiling it: sweets and screens can pass for loving yourself, and so can getting it out of anything hard.
source_quote: Treats and pampering do better at set times, where they can’t get out of hand. They shouldn’t get canceled as a punishment after a bad day, either.
why: The hypnosis guide names the slide into spoiling and gives no rule for treats, where the source now says to keep them to set times and not to cancel them as punishment.
what: After the spoiling sentence in S027.

hypnosis_quote: Work on developing a sense of who you are and reparent yourself as best you can.
source_quote: But if you grew up somewhere you only belonged as long as you played somebody else, like a really controlling family or a strict church, the real one may never have had room to form.
why: A reader whose inner child never appears is told what to do and not why it can happen, which the source now explains: where belonging meant playing someone else, the real child may never have had room to form.
what: S072, before the 'developing a sense of who you are' sentence.

hypnosis_quote: If you've had a similar experience, you know that there is a difference between having experienced it at one point, or only being able to access it in a certain state, and being able to get to it at any point in your life.
source_heading: What to Do With a Peak
source_quote: That night can’t be the bar for every morning after, or regular life starts to feel like failing. And gorgeous as it was, it doesn’t mean you’re done healing.
why: The reader is told to keep a peak experience as a reference point without the source's warning that it can't be the bar for ordinary days and doesn't mean the healing is done.
what: After the 'reference point' sentence in the third paragraph of S136.

hypnosis_quote: While you're building a way to reach love on a normal day, let that experience you had serve as a reference point for what can happen.
source_quote: Genuinely cultivated gratitude (not just empty/forced ritual) is one way to experience divine love for the first time, or to get it back when the feeling fades. I think it’s essential if we want to live in that love instead of occasionally visiting it.
why: The appendix speaks of building a way to reach love on a normal day and doesn't say how, where the source now gives gratitude as the everyday way in.
what: The 'reference point' sentence in S136.

hypnosis_quote: If you’re dealing with particularly complicated trauma, blind spots, dissociation, destabilization, or relational wounds that need another nervous system, skilled outside support may be best.
source_quote: I’d also want one who doesn’t put ideas in your head, and who understands dissociation, and can explain how they’d treat early sexual trauma if you have it, or whatever your specific trauma is.
why: The reader is told outside support may be best and not how to choose it, where the source now says what to ask a therapist, including whether they put ideas in your head.
what: The last sentence of S130; source S131 to S134 (Finding a Therapist).

hypnosis_quote: Check how much grown-up you is really in the room first.
source_quote: Some people get a little rush out of making somebody scared or small, though. For such folks, inner child therapy is clearly not the place to start.
why: The readiness check asks only whether enough adult is present, and misses the source's new screen for a reader who enjoys making someone scared or small, for whom this isn't the place to start.
what: Step A of S032.

hypnosis_quote: Tell your inner child or guard to write with your nondominant hand, and talk to them with your dominant.
source_quote: Lucia Capacchione, an art therapist and seminal inner child therapist, wrote a whole book on this one, The Power of Your Other Hand .
why: The reader isn't told the two-hand writing method is Lucia Capacchione's, which the source now credits with her book.
what: S034, and the sources list in S162.
